assessor: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Code), written 2026-10-18 after independently solving every item and before reading the earlier 2026-10-17 assessment. Advisory only: same provider family as the author of the drafts, so this is not independent evidence for any gate.
method: Reasoning demand for a strong Year 6 scholarship candidate: (1) number of distinct inferential or procedural steps, (2) whether the governing rule is given, familiar or must be discovered, (3) whether a trap, a second constraint or a search is needed. Marks, word count and reading load were deliberately not used as proxies. easy = one familiar idea or two routine steps; medium = a rule to discover or a translation into symbols plus two or three steps; challenging = several coordinated constraints or a non-routine search.

scholarship-y6-nr-003.label: easy
scholarship-y6-nr-003.rationale: Differences 2,4,6,8 follow one familiar growing-difference rule; take the differences once, extend once.

scholarship-y6-nr-004.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-004.rationale: The first differences (3,2,5,7) do not suggest a rule, so the candidate has to abandon the default method and discover that each term is the sum of the previous two.

scholarship-y6-nr-005.label: easy
scholarship-y6-nr-005.rationale: Two interleaved strands each move by a constant 3. Splitting the sequence is the only idea and it is routine for this cohort.

scholarship-y6-nr-007.label: easy
scholarship-y6-nr-007.rationale: Differences 3,6,9,12 are the multiples of three; one level of differences and an obvious pattern.

scholarship-y6-nr-008.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-008.rationale: First differences 2,6,10,14 are not constant, so a second level of differences (constant 4) must be found before extending.

scholarship-y6-nr-009.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-009.rationale: Two interleaved strands with different steps (+3 and -4) and a position trap: the next term belongs to the first strand, and the other strand's next value (38) is offered as a distractor. Borderline easy.

scholarship-y6-nr-010.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-010.rationale: Additive recurrence (each term is the sum of the previous two). Visible from 3+4=7, but it is a non-linear idea that most Year 6 candidates have not met. Borderline easy.

scholarship-y6-nr-012.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-012.rationale: No rule is stated. The candidate must hypothesise and test an invariant (every row and column sums to 30) before the missing cell can be found.

scholarship-y6-nr-021.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-021.rationale: Heads-and-legs needs an assume-all-chickens correction or a systematic trial with two coupled constraints; a classic but not a one-step item.

scholarship-y6-nr-026.label: easy
scholarship-y6-nr-026.rationale: Five consecutive numbers: the middle term is the mean (27), so the largest is 29. One shortcut, one step.

scholarship-y6-nr-030.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-030.rationale: Halve the perimeter, then solve a sum-and-difference pair and report the length rather than the width. Short, but three linked steps. Borderline easy.

scholarship-y6-nr-031.label: challenging
scholarship-y6-nr-031.rationale: Two coordinated constraints on the digits plus a quotient-and-remainder condition; the candidate has to build N = 7(t+u)+3 with t = u+3 and solve. Clearly the hardest item in the section.

scholarship-y6-nr-035.label: easy
scholarship-y6-nr-035.rationale: One unknown with direct relationships (M + M+4 + 2M = 44). The label is right; the estimator over-reads its word count.

scholarship-y6-nr-038.label: medium
scholarship-y6-nr-038.rationale: A short factor-pair search for sum 18 and product 72, then the difference. Borderline easy because the pair is found quickly.

scholarship-y6-maths-002.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-002.rationale: Three sequential signed changes with direction words. Several operations but one idea, so easy.

scholarship-y6-maths-003.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-003.rationale: A double negative inside a four-term expression; the sign handling, not the arithmetic, is the demand.

scholarship-y6-maths-008.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-008.rationale: Percentage difference (20%) of a total, or two simple percentages. Routine.

scholarship-y6-maths-010.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-010.rationale: Percentage increase on friendly numbers. The wrong-base trap (20%) is well known and is offered as a distractor.

scholarship-y6-maths-012.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-012.rationale: Share $72,000 in the ratio 2:3:4 and report the middle share. Standard.

scholarship-y6-maths-017.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-017.rationale: Ratio parts of a total with friendly numbers.

scholarship-y6-maths-019.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-019.rationale: Sum and difference of two ages with small numbers.

scholarship-y6-maths-020.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-020.rationale: Unknown on both sides of a given equation. Procedural, but collecting terms across the equals sign is above routine Year 6 work.

scholarship-y6-maths-021.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-021.rationale: Three consecutive odd numbers need either the mean shortcut (29, then +2) or x, x+2, x+4 set up and solved. The distractor 29 catches the slip. Borderline easy.

scholarship-y6-maths-022.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-022.rationale: Two linear conditions in two unknowns, solved by substitution or elimination. Arguably the hardest maths item in this group and could be argued up to challenging.

scholarship-y6-maths-023.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-023.rationale: Direct substitution; the only care needed is reading 2qr as a product and applying order of operations.

scholarship-y6-maths-025.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-025.rationale: A verbal description must be translated into 6n - 14 = 2n + 18, then solved with the unknown on both sides.

scholarship-y6-maths-026.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-026.rationale: Vertically opposite angles are equal, then an unknown-on-both-sides solve, then back-substitution to report the angle rather than x.

scholarship-y6-maths-027.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-027.rationale: All three angles must be expressed through one variable and summed to 180; the distractor 40 is the value of B, not A.

scholarship-y6-maths-029.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-029.rationale: Supplementary angles plus a careful translation of '36 less than three times'; the question asks for the smaller angle, so the other angle must be checked.

scholarship-y6-maths-031.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-031.rationale: Subtract one square area from another.

scholarship-y6-maths-032.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-032.rationale: Needs the polygon angle-sum rule or the exterior-angle idea, which is stretch content for Year 6; the arithmetic after that is easy.

scholarship-y6-maths-033.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-033.rationale: Complement probability as a percentage; the NOT in the stem is the only trap.

scholarship-y6-maths-035.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-035.rationale: Inclusion-exclusion (or a Venn diagram) to avoid double-counting the 7 who play both sports.

scholarship-y6-maths-037.label: easy
scholarship-y6-maths-037.rationale: A repeated change followed by one more; the result crosses zero but the arithmetic is two simple steps.

scholarship-y6-maths-039.label: medium
scholarship-y6-maths-039.rationale: Build a perimeter expression that counts the repeated side twice, collect terms, then solve for k.
